title: Wendell and the Terminal
premise: When gravity across the Halcyon system stutters for nine seconds, Lior Voss discovers the anomaly is a message: the ancient relay network that quietly governs all interstellar traffic has begun executing a dead founder's hidden will — one that redistributes control of every jump gate and names Lior's long-missing father as executor. Racing rival factions who want the inheritance buried, Lior must reach the terminal relay at the edge of dead space before the signal completes its transfer. In the end he learns his father chose him not as heir but as witness, and Lior must decide whether to hand power to the system's oppressed outer colonies or destroy it forever — choosing to shatter the network into pieces no single faction can own.
about_author: Elodie Eriksen is a former maritime radio operator from the Faroe Islands who writes science fiction about people who keep distant machines alive. Her work has appeared in several small-press anthologies exploring isolation, labor, and the ethics of inherited systems.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Falling
chapters.summary: Lior Voss, sole technician on relay station Kestrel-7, hauls cargo drones through contested orbits while rationing his last human contact. When gravity flickers for exactly nine seconds, every machine on the station logs the same impossible timestamp. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: loneliness cracked open by wonder.

chapters.title: The Message in the Mass
chapters.summary: Lior decodes the anomaly: the flicker was a handshake signal propagating through the ancient relay lattice, addressed to an executor named Voss. His father, missing twelve years, may be alive inside dead space. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: grief reignited into desperate hope.

chapters.title: Visitors with Clean Boots
chapters.summary: A corporate audit team from Meridian Combine arrives unannounced, asking oddly specific questions about gravitational telemetry. Lior lies badly and they leave a tracker behind. POV: Lior, with a brief interlude from auditor Sefa Idris. Emotional beat: paranoia taking root.

chapters.title: Cargo Run Through Contested Space
chapters.summary: Lior takes a routine haul toward the inner colonies but detours to a black-market contact, Juno Reyes, who confirms others received the nine-second pulse — and that Meridian is hunting anyone who knows. A pirate skiff shadows them home. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: the cost of curiosity made real.

chapters.title: What the Founder Built
chapters.summary: Juno reveals the relays were built by Aurelia Kade, whose 'death' a century ago was actually a retreat into the network itself. The pulse is her will executing at last. POV: Juno. Emotional beat: history reframed as unfinished business.

chapters.title: The Tracker Blooms
chapters.summary: Meridian seizes Kestrel-7 using the planted tracker; Lior escapes in a cargo pod during a staged decompression, watching three years of his life burn behind him. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: exile — grief for a home that was never really his.

chapters.title: Fleet of the Unclaimed
chapters.summary: Lior shelters with the Drift Compact, outer-colony salvagers who've been denied gate access for generations. Their leader, old Mabon, recognizes the Voss name and tells him what his father did for them. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: belonging offered where he least expects it.

chapters.title: Sefa's Report
chapters.summary: Auditor Sefa Idris, pressured to falsify findings, discovers Meridian plans to seize the entire relay lattice under emergency law. Her loyalty fractures. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: complicity curdling into conscience.

chapters.title: The Race Map
chapters.summary: Mabon lays out the geometry: the will's signal travels relay to relay and terminates at the Terminal in dead space. Whoever controls the Terminal when it arrives owns everything. Meridian's fast corvettes have a head start. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Bargaining with Pirates
chapters.summary: To outrun the corvettes, Lior trades the Compact's only jump-capable tug to smuggler captain Oyelaran for a patched-up courier ship — and a debt he can't name yet. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: the first true sacrifice.

chapters.title: Ghost Traffic
chapters.summary: In transit, Lior's ship receives messages routed through relays that shouldn't function: fragments of his father's voice, recorded years ago, guiding him along a route only a Voss would trust. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: intimacy with the dead, tender and unsettling.

chapters.title: The Checkpoint at Vell
chapters.summary: Meridian has militarized the Vell relay chokepoint. Sefa, now a defector, smuggles Lior's ship through inspection by falsifying her own manifests. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: crossing the line she can never uncross.

chapters.title: Interrogation of a Ghost
chapters.summary: Hiding in a comet shadow, Lior plays the full recording: his father confesses he helped Kade design the will, then fled rather than become its executor — and named Lior knowing the network would find him. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: fury at being used, and understanding anyway.

chapters.title: Meridian's Offer
chapters.summary: Oyelaran sells their position to Meridian. A boarding party offers Lior wealth and his station back if he surrenders his genetic key. He refuses; the Compact crew covers his escape, and Mabon dies holding the airlock. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: rage and mourning fused.

chapters.title: Dead Space
chapters.summary: Past the last functioning beacon, Lior flies blind through dead space with Sefa navigating by starlight and arithmetic. The silence strips away everything but the choice ahead. POV: alternating Lior and Sefa. Emotional beat: stripped-bare honesty between strangers.

chapters.title: The Terminal Appears
chapters.summary: They reach the Terminal: a cathedral-scale structure older than any colony, still warm after a century alone. Inside, dormant systems wake at Lior's presence like something inhaling. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: awe edged with terror.

chapters.title: Aurelia Kade's Will
chapters.summary: Kade's recorded testament explains everything: she built the network to serve everyone, watched corporations strangle it, and encoded a final transfer that would dissolve corporate gate rights and return them to the colonies — if an executor arrived in good faith. POV: Kade (recording). Emotional beat: a century of patience paying out.

chapters.title: Corvettes at the Door
chapters.summary: Meridian's fleet arrives; marines breach the Terminal while lawyers argue the transfer is legally void. Sefa holds them off with testimony and locked blast doors as the countdown to execution begins. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: courage without any guarantee.

chapters.title: The Executor's Choice
chapters.summary: At the console, Lior faces the final prompt: execute the transfer, claim the power himself, or abort. He sees his father's flaw — choosing heirs instead of witnesses — and chooses a fourth path: fragmentation, scattering gate authority among every colony that asks. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: the climax of conscience over power.

chapters.title: Everything Falls Open
chapters.summary: The network executes: gates unlock across the system, Meridian's monopoly dissolves mid-boardroom, and the corvettes lose their legal teeth even as their weapons stay hot. Lior triggers the Terminal's self-scatter, denying anyone the throne. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: release — the weight finally set down.

chapters.title: After the Signal
chapters.summary: Weeks later, the Compact runs its first independent convoy through an open gate. Sefa testifies before a provisional colonial assembly; Oyelaran, surprisingly, pays back the debt in fuel and silence. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: justice arriving imperfectly, but arriving.

chapters.title: Wendell and the Terminal
chapters.summary: Lior returns to rebuilt Kestrel-7 with a salvage AI he names Wendell, hauling cargo through orbits that belong to no one and everyone. The nine-second pulse echoes once more across the system — a heartbeat, not a summons. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: quiet peace earned, not granted.
